resources.string: Nucleus icons inside a muscle fiber
Starting nucleus icons inside the fiber
Final nucleus icons inside the fiber = starting nucleus icons + fused descendant icons. Separate reserve cell icons = 8 minus fused descendant icons. The chart rounds the controls to whole icons.

Muscle satellite cells sit beneath the basal lamina but outside the muscle fiber membrane. Some descendants can renew that reserve; muscle-forming descendants can fuse with a fiber and contribute their nuclei. The sketch starts with 8 descendant icons. Each one shown fusing adds a nucleus icon inside the fiber; this sketch puts all the others in the separate reserve. That split and the counts are invented, not fixed cell fates, real cell or nucleus counts, or predictions of repair.
